channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: SJC seeks amicus briefs in upcoming cases
item.description: The SJC is seeking amicus briefs in two upcoming cases.

item.title: Denial of motion to withdraw plea reversed by SJC
item.description: A defendant’s motion to withdraw his guilty plea on the basis that defense counsel failed to inform him that his plea rendered his deportation virtually mandatory should not have been denied without an evidentiary hearing, the Supreme Judicial Court has ruled in a split decision.

item.title: Civil practice – Witness tampering – Sanction
item.description: Where a U.S. magistrate judge dismissed a plaintiff’s complaint as a sanction for tampering with a witness, the dismissal order should be affirmed because (1) the magistrate judge reached a reasonable conclusion that there was clear and convincing evidence showing that the defendant improperly attempted to dissuade the witness from testifying and (2) it was not an abuse of discretion to order dismissal rather than a lesser sanction.

item.title: Appeals – G.L.c. 211, §3
item.description: Where a petitioner whose motion to dismiss a drunk driving charge was denied in District Court sought relief under G.L.c. 211, §3, a single justice’s decision to deny relief should be affirmed based on the availability of a remedy in the ordinary appellate process.

item.title: Criminal – Plea – Immigration consequences
item.description: Where (1) a defendant who pleaded guilty to possession of a controlled substance with intent to distribute filed a motion to withdraw his plea on the basis that plea counsel failed to inform him that his plea rendered his deportation virtually mandatory and (2) that motion was denied without an evidentiary hearing primarily on the basis that plea counsel's affidavit averring that he did not tell the defendant that he would be automatically deported was not credible because it was inconsistent wi

item.title: Tort – Harassment prevention order
item.description: Where a G.L.c. 258E harassment prevention order has been challenged on appeal, that order must be vacated because there was no evidence of a third qualifying act of harassment.

item.title: Real property – Constructive trust – Cohabitants
item.description: Where a plaintiff has filed a motion to amend her petition to specifically articulate claims of constructive trust and resulting trust, that motion should be allowed in part and denied in part, as the plaintiff’s resulting trust claims are futile, but her allegations are sufficient to raise her constructive trust claims above the speculative level.

item.title: Real property – ‘Lifetime occupancy agreement’
item.description: Where two plaintiffs have brought suit to enforce their “lifetime occupancy agreement” with the defendant, a motion by the defendant to dismiss the complaint should be denied because (1) three documents presented in an appendix to the motion to dismiss must be stricken because they were not referred to or relied on in the complaint and (2) without the facts found only in the stricken exhibits, the defendant’s motion to dismiss cannot succeed.

item.title: Immigration – Arrest – Interview
item.description: Where a plaintiff has requested a temporary restraining order based on his fear that he will be arrested upon showing up for a mandatory adjustment-of-status interview, the request should be granted in part, as the plaintiff has demonstrated a substantial likelihood of success on the merits of his claim that the defendants’ arrest-at-interview practice violates the Immigration and Nationality Act and the Administrative Procedure Act.

item.title: Attorneys – Malpractice
item.description: Where summary judgment was awarded to a defendant law firm, that judgment must be reversed in part, as the lower court erred by holding that the plaintiff’s legal malpractice claim was untimely as a matter of law and that no implied attorney-client relationship existed between the plaintiff and the law firm.
